subject: Conversation stream: token emission gaps — notice, triage, and runbook
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@apexai.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-06T12:15:00-05:00
Subject: Conversation stream emitting tokens with long gaps — observed 2-4s pauses

Hi Rishi,

Today between ~11:30–12:00 ET we started seeing long pauses in the streaming responses from Redwood's chat endpoint. Tokens come in bursts, then gaps of ~2–4s. This is causing the typing indicator in our client to hang and degrade the UX. Examples attached (small trace and timestamps).

Can you confirm if anything changed on Redwood's side? We're on a standard Hosted plan and haven't modified our client. This is affecting a handful of customer sessions (trace ids listed below).

Trace ids: 2c9f-7a88, 2c9f-7a92
App environment: prod us-east-1
Contact: liam.oconnor@apexai.com

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform — ApexAI
liam.oconnor@apexai.com
Attachments: streaming_trace_2c9f-7a88.txt (log), timestamps.csv (CSV)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@apexai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-06T12:35:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Conversation stream emitting tokens with long gaps — initial triage and immediate workarounds

Hi Liam — thanks for flagging and for the traces.

We're looking into this now. Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm if you were using streaming with chunked=true and a model pin? (yes/no)
- If possible, capture an HTTP-level pcap for one of the sessions.

Short-term mitigations you can try now:
- Use non-streaming (complete response) as a fallback for the affected endpoint (switching to polling).
- Reduce max_tokens_per_chunk in the client to 64.

I'll loop in our ops team and follow up within 60 minutes with a status. Apologies for the disruption — we'll prioritize this.

Best,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: (none)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-06T13:00:00-05:00
Subject: Fwd: Conversation stream emitting tokens with long gaps — triage + action items

Team — forwarding ApexAI report. Key context:
- Customer seeing 2–4s token emission gaps in us-east-1 streaming.
- Affected traces 2c9f-7a88 and 2c9f-7a92.
- Appears during sustained interactive sessions at ~150–200 RPS per cluster.

Initial observations from infra:
- Edge proxies intermittently returning partial frames; possible backpressure/backoff between proxy and inference shard.
- KV-cache miss storms noted around 11:25–11:40 ET on edge shard 12.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Monica: bump streaming proxy soft-concurrency for shard 12 by +25% and monitor token inter-arrival.
2) Laura: roll a temporary canary that disables prefix-prefetch for the affected shard to avoid cache thrash.
3) Ben: prepare a mitigation note for the customer with three client-side workarounds (poll fallback, reduce tokens/chunk, exponential retry jitter).

Also collect:
- proxy logs for shard 12 11:00–12:00 ET
- application-level emit timestamps (customer traces exist)

I'll take point on customer comms. Please update within 15 minutes if you see obvious regressions.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@apexai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T09:20:00-05:00
Subject: Resolution and post-incident guidance — token emission gaps (us-east-1)

Hi Liam,

Quick update and summary of actions we took overnight — thank you again for the traces, they were helpful.

What happened (short): during a maintenance window we deployed an edge routing change that caused a transient KV-cache miss storm on a subset of edge shards in us-east-1. That increased backend latency spikes and produced visible gaps in streaming token emission.

What we did:
- Increased streaming proxy soft-concurrency on affected shards to relieve backpressure.
- Deployed a targeted rollback of the routing rule that triggered prefix-prefetch storms.
- Tuned the max-inflight request threshold for the inference pool serving the relevant model variant.

Customer-facing mitigations (recommended):
- If you need an immediate safer behavior during peak periods: switch to non-streaming completes for critical sessions or enable client-side polling for up to 5s timeouts.
- Lower max_tokens_per_chunk to 64 to reduce the chance of observable pauses.
- Add client-side exponential jitter to reconnect attempts (sample snippet attached).

We've attached a short runbook (apexai_mitigation_runbook.pdf) and the relevant trace aggregation (trace-2c9f-7a88-20261206.log). We'll continue to monitor and will run a postmortem next week; I can share the timeline and root cause with your engineering leads.

If you'd like a short sync to walk through the runbook, I can schedule time this week.

Apologies again for the disruption — we aim to keep streaming behavior smooth and predictable. Let me know if the mitigations help.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments: apexai_mitigation_runbook.pdf (pdf), trace-2c9f-7a88-20261206.log (log)
